name: MeltFlex
summary: AI interior design tool. Its dorm planner furnishes an uploaded photo of your dorm room as a single, double or triple in a chosen layout and look, with real retailer furniture available.
how_it_works: Upload a photo of your dorm room (or use an example photo), pick single, double or triple, a layout and an optional decor look, then the AI renders the furnished room in under 30 seconds.

facts.free_tier: Free plan, no credit card required; includes the IKEA catalog; free renders carry a small MeltFlex watermark (pricing page data: 15 credits, 3 projects)
facts.shopping: Real furniture from 9 retailers (IKEA, Wayfair, Amazon, Pottery Barn, Ashley Furniture, Walmart, West Elm, Costco, Rooms To Go) with prices and retailer links; free plan has the IKEA catalog only

sources.quote: Upload a photo of your dorm room, then pick single, double or triple, a layout and a look
Upload a photo of the room and MeltFlex AI furnishes it as a single, double or triple, with lofted beds, bunks, mirrored halves or a divider, in the look you pick, in under 30 seconds.
Don't have a photo right now? You can use one of our example photos
Is the dorm room planner free? Yes. You can upload a photo and generate a dorm room design for free, with no account needed to get started.
Your first dorm render is free, no credit card needed.

name: Planner 5D
summary: Home and interior design software for 2D/3D floor plans and room layouts, plus an AI Studio that restyles an uploaded room photo. Its dorm page covers student rooms and student-housing planning.
how_it_works: Create a room at scale (start from scratch, enter dimensions, or upload a floor plan), place beds, desks and storage, and compare layouts in 2D and 3D; or upload a dorm photo to AI Studio and describe changes.

facts.free_tier: Free plan: $0, unlimited projects, 50% of the furniture catalog, web and mobile; no time limit
facts.shopping: In-app catalog of 10,000+ furniture items (half free); separate shop.planner5d.com lists third-party retailers' products, purchases completed on the retailer's site

name: Spoak
summary: A subscription-based, ad-free web studio for interior design lovers: to-scale floor plans, room mockups and mood boards built with real products, plus a design community.
how_it_works: Set a budget, sign up, draw a to-scale floor plan (from scratch, a template, or an uploaded plan), shop or import products into it, and add a roommate as a collaborator for feedback.

facts.free_tier: Free Guest pass: $0, no credit card, 1,000 starter tokens, one design in each mode; designs lock from editing after 24 hours
facts.shopping: Shop products inside Spoak; import products from any website via Chrome extension or auto-import; budget and shop-list tracking

name: 101 Planners Dorm Room Planner
summary: A free, browser-based dorm layout tool on 101planners.com: drag dorm-sized furniture onto a to-scale floor plan, get layout warnings, tag items by owner, and export the plan.
how_it_works: Pick a room size (presets or custom), drag dorm furniture onto the floor plan, fix the problems it flags, tag each piece as yours, your roommate's or shared, then save as an image or PDF to send.

facts.free_tier: Entirely free: no sign-up, no account, no email, no paid tier; plan saves in your browser

sources.quote: You pick your room size, drag furniture onto a to-scale floor plan, and move it around until it works.
As you go, it tells you what is broken: a dresser sitting in the swing of the door, a wardrobe blocking the only window, two things occupying the same square foot of floor, three people and two beds.
Then you save it as an image or a PDF and send it to the person you are going to be living with.
It is free, it does not ask for an email, and it saves your plan in your browser so you can come back to it.
Yes. There is no sign-up, no account, no email required, and no paid tier. Your plan saves automatically in your browser, so you can close the tab and come back to it.

A standard double runs about 12 by 15 feet, or roughly 180 square feet. A small double is closer to 10 by 12, about 120 square feet, and it is tight enough that lofting stops being a preference and becomes the plan.
If your school publishes room dimensions, start there. Many housing sites list square footage and floor plans by building, and residence life will usually tell you if you email and ask.
Once you have real numbers, enter them as a custom size and the whole layout rescales.
So the planner tags every piece of furniture as yours, your roommate’s, or shared, and colour-codes the floor plan accordingly. Then you export it and send it to them.
Yes. Dragging works with touch the same way it works with a mouse.
Yes. You can save it as an image, download it as a PDF, or print it directly.
